sections.html:
Lake County has no stand-alone recorder. The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office handles deeds, on the 6th floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Deeds are accepted in person or by mail.

The division's phone is 847-377-2575 and its fax is 847-984-5860. A recorded deed gets a document number, is scanned and entered in a grantor and grantee index, and the original goes back to the party named on the document. The office closes for holidays such as Thanksgiving, so confirm with the staff if your closing depends on same-day recording. The staff do not replace legal or accounting advice about the effect of a deed change.

Lake County is in the northeast corner of Illinois, with Waukegan as seat and largest city. Population is about 719,339, the median home value is $345,700, and owners live in 74.8% of homes. At those values, a clean deed and a smooth recording matter to a buyer's lender.

A deed is a standard document in Lake County, and a standard document costs $70. The only extra charges collected at recording are the state and county real estate transfer taxes that come due on a sale.

Lake County Clerk recording fees by document type
DocumentFee
Standard document, including most deeds$70
Standard document from a government agency exempt from the rental housing surcharge$50
Non-standard document$82
Non-standard document from an exempt government agency$62
Federal or state lien, lien release, UCC termination$43
UCC-1 and UCC-3 filings$58

Copies of recorded documents are $1 per page, plats are $5 per page, and a PTAX form is $1. Military discharges are free to the veteran. The office takes cash, checks made out to the Lake County Clerk, and Discover, MasterCard or Visa.

The Clerk applies the definition in 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1, and anything outside it is treated as standard. Six situations push a document into the higher fee:

  • It divides an active tax parcel number into new parcels
  • It is recorded under the Uniform Commercial Code
  • It does not meet the paper and layout rules, such as 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, black ink, white 20-pound paper, half-inch margins and a blank 3 by 5 inch space at the upper right of page one
  • It is a state or federal lien
  • It refers to more than 5 tax parcel numbers in the county
  • It refers to more than 5 other recorded document numbers

A deed printed cleanly on letter paper, with no staples on attachments and no more than five parcel numbers, stays at the $70 level.

The county's recording pamphlet lists ten requirements, and a deed missing one is likely to be turned back. In short:

  • It is dated, signed and notarized
  • The parties are named, with the buyer's address
  • It carries a full legal description, plus a Plat Act affidavit if the description uses metes and bounds
  • It shows the preparer's name and address
  • It gives a mail-to name and address for the return of the recorded deed
  • It lists the taxpayer name and address for future tax bills
  • It comes with a completed PTAX-203 or a signed and dated exemption statement
  • It has any municipal transfer stamps obtained beforehand

Titles to mobile homes are not recorded here. In Illinois those are registered with the Secretary of State, which has offices in Deerfield, Lake Zurich and Waukegan.

Lake County collects two transfer taxes at recording. The state rate is 50 cents per $500 and the county rate is 25 cents per $500, figured on the PTAX-203. The state rate matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15, and paper stamps have given way to electronic stamps or similar proof of payment.

The state's MyDec website prepares the PTAX-203 online. A transfer that qualifies for an exemption carries a signed, dated exemption statement on the deed instead.

Local stamps are a separate matter. Deeds for property in or mailing to Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa or North Chicago require a stamp or a signed exemption certificate from that municipality before the deed goes to the Clerk. Contact the municipal office first, since the Clerk will not obtain it for you.

Most deeds are eligible for eRecording through the Clerk's Speed eRecord service, and authorized business submitters prepare packages through CSC, eRecording Partners Network, Hopdox or Simplifile. Staff review each package and either approve it or send it back with the reason. A clean package can be recorded within minutes.

Two limits apply. Deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot go through the system, so an electronic deed needs a MyDec declaration. And deeds for the six municipalities above need the stamp or exemption certificate before submission. The standard recording fees apply, and the vendors add their own processing fee.

Individual homeowners generally go through a title company or attorney rather than opening an account themselves.

The county's pamphlet defines the common forms. Sole ownership leaves no other person with an interest. Joint tenancy gives two or more people equal undivided interests, and when one dies the share passes to the surviving joint tenants rather than to heirs. Tenancy by the entirety is a form for spouses that passes the whole property to the survivor without probate. Tenancy in common allows unequal shares and carries no right of survivorship.

The attorney who prepares the deed decides which form fits. A sale deed usually names the seller as grantor in whichever form title is currently held.

sections.h2: Before you go to the counter
sections.html:
If you are recording without a title company, check the list above against your deed one line at a time. Confirm the PTAX-203 is complete, any municipal stamp is attached, and no more than five parcel numbers appear. Bring a check made out to the Lake County Clerk for the $70 fee plus the transfer taxes, or use a card. When a lender or buyer will want the recorded deed back, the mail-to address on the deed is where the original returns, so double-check it. A cash sale uses the same recording steps, and the title company usually files for you.

Allow time for mail, too. A deed sent by post is recorded when the division processes it, not when you mail it, so a closing with a firm date is better served by delivering the deed in person or by eRecording. Keep a copy of everything you hand over, and note the document number once it is assigned. That number is what you quote when you order a copy later, at $1 per page.

faqs.q: Is there a Recorder of Deeds office?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is run as the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office at 18 N County Street, 6th floor, in Waukegan. The phone is 847-377-2575.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $70 for a standard document, which covers most deeds. A non-standard document costs $82, and the only other charges at recording are the transfer taxes due on a sale.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents per $500 and the county rate is 25 cents per $500. Six municipalities, including Highland Park and Lake Forest, also require their own stamp or exemption before recording.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed with a paper PTAX-203 through eRecording?
faqs.a: No. Deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted through eRecording, so an electronic deed needs a MyDec declaration instead.

faqs.q: Where are mobile home titles recorded?
faqs.a: They are not recorded with the Clerk. Illinois registers mobile home titles through the Secretary of State, with offices in Deerfield, Lake Zurich and Waukegan.
